reason: Directly identifies TYR gene mutations (G301R, G227W) responsible for siamese and burmese phenotypes of the albino locus in domestic cats, and characterises TYRP1 variants for the brown locus. Core molecular genetics of TYR gene function.

Demonstrates that alphaB-crystallin (CRYAB/HSPB5) inhibits autoproteolytic maturation of caspase-3 in both mitochondrial and death-receptor apoptotic pathways and co-immunoprecipitates with the p24 caspase-3 intermediate in vivo. Direct mechanistic study of CRYAB protein function explaining its anti-apoptotic role.
Characterises a far-upstream cell-specific enhancer of the mouse TYR gene conferring high-level, copy-number-related expression in transgenic mice. Direct study of TYR transcriptional regulation.

Investigates TYR mutations in transgenic albino mice that develop amelanotic melanoma and unexpectedly acquire pigmentation; demonstrates tyrosinase activity and protein despite the original nucleotide 291 mutation. Direct TYR gene and protein study in a disease context.

Reports microinjection of mouse tyrosinase minigene (mg-Tyrs-J) into BALB/c albino mice yielding heritable patterned and uniform coat-colour phenotypes. Direct study of TYR gene expression and pigmentation regulation in vivo.

Maps P-region (S5-S6 loop) accessibility and gating function of the bovine retinal CNG channel using cysteine-substituted residues - this is the CNGA1/RCNC1 channel whose mutations cause retinitis pigmentosa (RP49). Direct structural-functional study of the CNGA1 protein in retinal tissue.

Case report of red-tinted contact lens use in a child with achromatopsia, a disease primarily caused by CNGA3 mutations. Describes clinical outcomes including visual acuity, contrast sensitivity, and quality of life. Directly addresses clinical management of CNGA3-related retinal disease.

Characterises the substrate specificity of alpha-crystallin as a molecular chaperone in the ocular lens context, showing it recognises non-native intermediates on the denaturation pathway. Direct study of CRYAB protein chaperone function that underlies why mutations lead to cataract and other lens pathologies.

Abstract is empty, but the title describes ectopic expression of alphaB-crystallin (CRYAB/HSPB5) in CHO cells suggesting a nuclear function for this protein. Direct study of CRYAB localisation and function; medium confidence due to missing abstract.

Abstract is empty, but the title describes biochemical characterisation of human hairbulb tyrosinase comparing normal and albino enzyme properties. Direct study of TYR enzyme; medium confidence due to missing abstract.

Abstract is empty, but the title covers glucocorticoid induction of small heat shock proteins in satellite cells in the context of desmin-related myopathy involving the R120G alphaB-crystallin (CRYAB) mutation - a known pathogenic CRYAB variant. Directly studies CRYAB mutation consequences; medium confidence due to missing abstract.

Describes a three-generation family with cone-rod dystrophy carrying a heterozygous CRX deletion [c.(100+1_101-1)_(c.900+1_?)del] that segregates with disease; characterises the arcuate temporal macular lesion phenotype. Direct CRX mutation/phenotype study.

Identifies two novel homozygous CRB1 missense mutations (c.1997T>A and c.2426A>C) in two Chinese consanguineous families with autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa and validates segregation in family members and 1260 controls. Direct CRB1 mutation spectrum study.

Cell Science at a Glance review of N-terminal acetyltransferases covering NAA10 and NAA15 (NatA complex subunits), their substrate coverage, cellular roles and disease connections. Directly relevant to both NAA10 and NAA15 genes in the library.

GWAS of iris and skin pigmentation in East Asians finds genome-wide significant association at the OCA2 region driven by the non-synonymous rs1800414 variant explaining up to 11.9% of iris colour variance. Direct OCA2 genetics study of a trait it mediates.

Abstract is empty, but the title describes complex genetic architecture of skin pigmentation in Africans - a study expected to involve OCA2 and SLC24A5 loci. Relevant given both genes are pigmentation loci; medium confidence due to missing abstract.

Demonstrates that SNPs in the OCA2/HERC2 region (rs12913832, rs1129038, rs916977) that determine eye colour are significantly associated with uveal melanoma risk (OR ~0.5, p < 1e-7). Directly implicates OCA2 as a uveal melanoma susceptibility locus with ophthalmic relevance.

Describes a directional Wnt/beta-catenin-Sox2-proneural pathway that coordinates the transition from proliferation to differentiation in the Xenopus retina, with Sox2 having dual roles in promoting competence and inhibiting differentiation via Notch. Direct study of SOX2 in retinal development.

Mechanistically characterises SOX1/2/3 regulatory target selection, showing that the proximal C-terminal domain of SOX2 specifically interacts with a partner factor that determines target specificity. Direct study of SOX2 molecular mechanism relevant to understanding how SOX2 mutations affect transcription in microphthalmia and anophthalmia.

Shows that SOX2 maintains quiescent progenitor state of postnatal retinal Muller glia; conditional Sox2 knockout disrupts radial morphology and cell-cycle quiescence, causing Muller cell depletion and retinal degeneration rescued partly by Notch induction. Direct study of SOX2 in retinal biology.
